summary:
Martian Duck is a layered, integrated 3D map of a Marswalk route in Jezero Crater. Astronauts can plan the walk on it, rehearse it in first person (through the astronaut helmet), and carry it out. It covers the western half of the crater (45 × 59 km) at true scale, under Mars gravity, and combines data from three NASA missions:

Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter: CTX elevation model and photo mosaic for the terrain, and CRISM hydrous-mineral detections as a toggleable layer.
Mars Global Surveyor: the TES Dust Cover Index, which marks dusty ground that is risky to walk on.
Mars 2020 Perseverance: the rover’s drive path and tracks, real sampling sites and the sample depot, with Mastcam-Z and WATSON photos at each stop.

The explorer picks destinations on the map. A planner then finds the fastest safe route: A* search with walking speed from Tobler’s hiking function, a 30° slope limit, avoidance of dusty ground, and the best order to visit the stops. A helmet HUD guides the walk with navigation, a compass, waypoints and data layers. A science mission, “Follow the water,” leads the explorer from igneous rock to water-altered rock to a potential biosignature site.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
Martian Duck is a layered, interactive 3D map for planning and carrying out a Marswalk in Jezero Crater, where NASA’s Perseverance rover landed. It covers the western half of the crater (45 x 59 km) at true scale, including the delta, the crater rim and the Three Forks sample depot. The explorer walks it in first person under Mars gravity.

HOW IT WORKS
Data from several missions sits in one georeferenced frame. The terrain is the Mars 2020 CTX elevation model and photo mosaic (Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter). Toggleable layers show hydrous- and aqueous-mineral detections from NASA Mars Trek (CRISM/OMEGA) and the TES Dust Cover Index (Mars Global Surveyor). Perseverance’s real drive path is rendered as rover tracks, with its sampling sites, the sample depot, and raw rover images at each stop.

On the map, the explorer picks destinations. An A* route planner then finds the fastest safe walk over the 4097 x 4097 height grid. Walking time is the cost, using Tobler’s hiking function. Ground steeper than 30 degrees is excluded and ground near that limit is penalised. Dusty ground costs extra. With several stops, the planner chooses the best visiting order. It reports distance, climb, maximum slope and time, and re-plans when the explorer strays. A helmet HUD guides the walk with navigation, a compass, waypoints and data layers.

Two missions give the walk a science purpose. The first retrieves the depot’s sample tubes. The second, “Follow the water,” drills four real Perseverance sites in order, from igneous rock, through water-formed carbonate, to the potential biosignature rock Cheyava Falls.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Astronauts on Mars will have limited time, oxygen and margin for error. This map shows in one view whether a route is walkable, how long it takes, and what science lies along it. It works both for mission rehearsal and for public outreach.

TOOLS
Unity 6 (URP), C#, the Input System and UI Toolkit. A Python pipeline (GDAL, NumPy, Pillow) crops the orbital data, builds the mineral and rover-track layers, and fetches rover images from NASA’s public feed. Git LFS stores the large assets. It runs on a standard PC or Mac.

CREATIVITY
Most Mars maps are static 2D layers. This one puts you on the ground at true scale. The planner models human walking (speed, slope, footing) rather than straight lines, and the science mission follows the history of water at Jezero.

FIELD AR TABLET SOFTWARE (PROOF OF CONCEPT)
We also built a proof-of-concept AR application for a tablet that astronauts could carry on a Marswalk. The desktop map is used to plan and rehearse the walk. The tablet brings that plan into the field and overlays guidance on the astronaut’s real view: [e.g. the planned route, the next waypoint, hazards such as steep or dusty ground, and information about nearby sampling sites]. This connects planning and execution: the route chosen on the map is the route followed on the ground.

FACTORS CONSIDERED
The 20 m elevation model smooths out small hazards, so the planner keeps a safety margin from the slope limit. The dust data is coarse (about 3.6 km per pixel), so it steers between broad regions only. Searches are coarsened and spread across frames so the game stays responsive. Every layer comes from public data and is credited.

NEXT STEPS
The radiation and suit panels currently use placeholder values. We plan to connect them to real data (Curiosity RAD dose rates, MEDA weather) so the map also covers current conditions.
